questions.q: Long-range **weather forecasting and nuclear simulation** are typical applications of —
questions.solution: One gigantic scientific computation at a time is the supercomputer's job — weather models, nuclear simulations, space and defence research.

questions.q: PARAM 8000, India's first indigenous supercomputer (1991), was developed by:
questions.solution: PARAM 8000 was built in 1991 by C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing), Pune, under Dr Vijay Bhatkar, after the USA denied Cray supercomputer imports.
questions.shortcut: PARAM always pairs with C-DAC; the denial story (' PARAM = Perform Anvaya Reusable Module') is extra trivia - the developer is what SSC asks.

questions.q: The **RJ-45** socket on a computer is used for —
questions.solution: **RJ-45** is the Ethernet port — the tabbed socket that accepts the LAN cable.

questions.q: Entering a single quote followed by SQL code into a login form to manipulate the database is:
questions.solution: SQL injection feeds crafted SQL through input fields so the database executes attacker logic - usually a symptom of unvalidated input.

questions.q: Select the word which is nearest in meaning to the given word.  MALICIOUS
questions.solution: mal = bad → intending harm → **spiteful**. The other options fail the direction check: a mal- word must be negative.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

At the drop of a hat
questions.solution: A dropped hat was the instant signal to begin a fight or race → **immediately, without needing any reason**. 'Reluctance' and 'planning' contradict the idiom's whole point.
questions.shortcut: Signal picture: hat drops, action starts.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: **Rarely** makes the statement negative, so the tag must be positive: **does he?** 'Doesn't he' fails to flip — the same trap hides behind never, seldom, hardly and little.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The students decorated the classroom ___.
questions.solution: The students did it without help, which calls for the reflexive of 'they': **themselves**. 'Theirselves' and 'themself' are non-standard, and 'ourselves' does not match the subject.

questions.q: Harappan buildings used **burnt bricks** in the ratio —
questions.solution: Bricks everywhere followed the fixed ratio **width : height : length = 1 : 2 : 4**, a sign of standardisation across the civilisation.

questions.q: India's **inflation target** for monetary policy is —
questions.solution: The flexible inflation target is **4% CPI, ±2%** — set under the 2016 framework; breaching the band for three straight quarters forces a written report to the government.

questions.q: The Olympic motto 'Citius, Altius, Communius' adds which idea?
questions.solution: **Communius = 'Together'**, added in 2021 to 'Faster, Higher, Stronger' — the newest static layer of the motto.

questions.q: Which is the southernmost and youngest range of the Himalayas?
questions.solution: The **Shiwalik** (Outer Himalaya) is the lowest, youngest and southernmost range, made of loose river sediments.

questions.q: A cask is full of wine. 8 litres are drawn and replaced with water; the operation is performed three more times. The ratio of wine to water is finally 16:65. The capacity of the cask is:
questions.solution: Wine fraction $= \frac{16}{81} = \left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^4$ → $1-\frac{8}{C} = \frac{2}{3}$ → $C = 24$ L.
questions.shortcut: Four operations in all → fourth root; 16:65 pairs wine with water, so use $\frac{16}{81}$.

questions.q: Four years ago, the ages of A and B were in the ratio 3 : 5. Four years from now, the ratio will be 5 : 7. The sum of their present ages is:
questions.solution:
Four years ago: 3x, 5x; four years hence: $3x + 8$, $5x + 8$.
$\frac{3x + 8}{5x + 8} = \frac{5}{7}$ → $21x + 56 = 25x + 40$ → $x = 4$.
Ages now: 16 and 24 → sum $= 40$ years.

questions.q: The greatest value of $7+4x-x^2$ is:
questions.solution: $-(x-2)^2+11$ → greatest value 11 at $x=2$.

questions.q: If 3 men or 5 women can complete a piece of work in 12 days, then 6 men and 5 women together will complete it in:
**D is 6 km West of C. C is 4 km South of B.** In which direction is **B from D**?
questions.solution: Place D at the origin. 'D is 6 km West of C' puts C 6 km **East** of D. 'C is 4 km South of B' puts B 4 km **North** of C. So B sits at (+6, +4) from D → **North-East** of D.
questions.shortcut: Anchor at D (the asked-from point); C hangs East, B hangs North of C.

questions.q: In a certain code, **PAINT** is written as **UOJBQ**. How is **BRUSH** written in that code?
questions.solution: PAINT reversed = TNIAP; T→U (+1), N→O (+1), I→J (+1), A→B (+1), P→Q (+1) → reverse, then +1. BRUSH reversed = HSURB; +1 → **ITVSC**.
questions.shortcut: First code letter U = T + 1, and T is the last letter of PAINT → reversal + 1.

questions.q:
Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out. (The letters follow English alphabetical order.)

**BHL, DJP, FNT, GLR**
questions.solution: Positions: B(2) H(8) L(12); D(4) J(10) P(16); F(6) N(14) T(20) - every letter is at an **even** position. G(7) is odd in GLR → **GLR**.

questions.q: Pointing to a boy, Neha said, **"His mother is the only daughter of my mother."** How is Neha related to the boy?
questions.solution: My mother's only daughter = Neha herself (her mother has exactly one daughter). So the boy's mother **is** Neha → Neha is his **mother**.
questions.shortcut: 'Only daughter of my mother' is the speaker, whenever the speaker is female.
